messages.subject: predict.oSCR error
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Just trying to make a map of density from top model.

Getting an error I haven’t been able to troubleshoot. Any ideas?

> rast <- predict.oSCR(scrFrame=ms.sf, top.mod, ms.ssDF)
Error in ifelse(se, TRUE, FALSE) :
  promise already under evaluation: recursive default argument reference or earlier problems?

Cheers,
Clayton
--
Clayton Lamb, PhD Candidate
South Rockies Grizzly Bear Project
S.Boutin and S.Nielsen Labs
Biological Sciences, University of Alberta

messages.subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] [oscr] predict.oSCR error
messages.body_plain:
Thanks,

Yes I originally inspected the source code (https://rdrr.io/github/jaroyle/oSCR/src/R/predict.oSCR.R) but didn’t see that error, must be a dependent function inside.

The only difference between this and another time that I’ve successfully used the predict.oSCR function is that the top.mod was extracted from an oSCR.parfit() run. But that shouldn’t be an issue I don’t think.

get.real(top.mod,
                     type = "dens”,….

Works just fine.

CL

messages.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] [oscr] predict.oSCR error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Clayton,

Actually, the parfit thing might be the issue. If you use parfit, the model names weren’t being saved correctly. I added a fix for that, and thought I checked all the functions that depended on that object, but apparently not. I think this is an easy fix, and can do that today (any chance you could send me the parfit object offline? Will be easier for me to reproduce, diagnose and fix).

(I’m sure you know this, but note that the expected density surfaces from get.real and the realized surfaces from predict.oscr, are different – I think you are aware of that though)

Apologies!!

Chris

Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] [oscr] predict.oSCR error

Yes I originally inspected the source code (https://rdrr.io/github/jaroyle/oSCR/src/R/predict.oSCR.R) but didn’t see that error, must be a dependent function inside.

The only difference between this and another time that I’ve successfully used the predict.oSCR function is that the top.mod was extracted from an oSCR.parfit() run. But that shouldn’t be an issue I don’t think.

get.real(top.mod,

                     type = "dens”,….

Works just fine.

CL

messages.body_plain:
Okay, this has revealed some things I need to work on with the oSCR.parfit() function. However, in the meantime, the following code and attached tmp.predict.oSCR() temporary fix should get you moving. This works fine and produced what you want IF and ONLY IF you are using the default argument values of oSCR.fit().

library(oSCR)

source("tmp.predict.oSCR.R")   #attached

fl <- readRDS("for_Chris.rds") #a fitList.oSCR object

pred1 <- tmp.predict.oSCR(fl[[1]])

I plan on getting this figured out more generally very soon, but needs a bit of brain power and some testing across dependent functions.

Chris
